stages.name: Scarcity
stages.title: Scarcity
stages.sub: Why every economy has to choose between competing uses of limited resources.

steps.text: A bakery needs flour, which is grown on fields and milled from wheat. Natural resources like this, used in production, are called
The bakers who knead the dough and work the ovens provide
The ovens and mixing machines the bakery uses are
The owner who brings the fields, bakers and ovens together and takes the risk provides

steps.prompt: Drag and drop the 4 key terms in the order they are used in production.

steps.q: Could the bakery ever have an endless supply of fields, bakers, ovens and owners, all at once?
steps.wrong: Yes, if the bakery grows big enough
steps.hint: Think about the whole country, not just one bakery. Is there an endless amount of any of these?

steps.q: If the fields, bakers and ovens are limited, what happens to the number of loaves that can ever be baked?
steps.right: There is a limit to how many can be made
steps.wrong: There is no limit, more can always be squeezed out
steps.hint: Loaves are made from these resources. If the resources run out, what happens to the loaves?
steps.pre: So the loaves, and every good and service, are

steps.q: A family finally buys the car they saved years for. A month later, do they stop wanting anything else?
steps.right: No, they soon want something new
steps.wrong: Yes, they have everything they need now
steps.hint: Think about what happens after you finally get something you really wanted.

steps.q: There are limited loaves, ovens and workers, but people always want more. Can everyone have all they want?
steps.wrong: Yes, if resources are used efficiently
steps.hint: Limited goods on one side, unlimited wants on the other: can both sides ever match up for everyone?
